page: Oracle Cloud Infrastructure VM.Optimized3.Flex.2-8 is a compute-focused virtual machine instance built on the Intel Xeon 6354 processor running at a base clock speed of 3.0 GHz. The instance configuration provisions 2 physical x86_64 cores supporting 4 dedicated vCPUs via multithreading. It includes 8.0 GB of system memory, providing a 1:2 vCPU-to-RAM ratio of 2.0 GB per core. The hardware architecture features 32 KB of L1 data cache, 4 MB of L2 cache, and 16 MB of shared L3 cache, alongside support for instruction sets including AVX-512, AVX-512 VNNI, and cryptographic acceleration through AES and SHA-NI.

The instance does not bundle local NVMe or SSD storage and relies on external block storage volumes for persistent data. Hardware acceleration via GPUs is not present. Network connectivity includes a single complimentary public IPv4 address. Benchmarks reflect balanced single-thread execution, showing average tier performance in single-core Geekbench (1660.0), stress-ng CPU execution, single-threaded gzip compression, and text generation on small language models. Conversely, multi-threaded throughput and memory bandwidth fall into lower percentiles, characterized by weak scores in multi-core Geekbench (3574.0), PassMark CPU execution, and high-load decompression tasks.

Cost efficiency is achieved by pairing high base clock frequencies with a lean memory footprint, avoiding the resource overhead of oversized RAM allocations or local storage drives. This profile suits latency-sensitive web serving, single-threaded processing pipelines, lightweight microservices, and general compute tasks that do not exceed the 8.0 GB memory envelope.
description: Oracle Cloud Infrastructure VM.Optimized3.Flex.2-8 is an x86_64 compute-oriented virtual machine featuring 4 dedicated vCPUs derived from 2 physical cores on an Intel Xeon 6354 processor running at 3.0 GHz. The system provides 8.0 GB of RAM, allocating 2.0 GB per core in a compute-aligned 1:2 vCPU-to-memory configuration. It contains no local disk storage or GPU accelerators, relying on remote volumes for persistence while providing one complimentary public IPv4 address. Benchmark results demonstrate consistent mid-tier single-core execution alongside lower multi-core scaling, reflected in average single-thread Geekbench and gzip results contrasted with weak multi-core and memory bandwidth metrics. VM.Optimized3.Flex.2-8 is targeted at CPU-bound tasks with modest memory requirements, such as web servers, lightweight microservices, and single-threaded batch processing.
